signs.heading: Signs You Need a Plumber
signs.line: Every one of these points back to a service above. If you're seeing any of them in your home, it's worth a call before it becomes a bigger job.

items.title: A Drain That Keeps Clogging
items.text: One clog is normal. The same drain clogging every few weeks usually means buildup deeper in the line, a partial obstruction, or a problem in the main sewer line. Plunging and store-bought drain cleaners treat the symptom and can damage older pipes.

items.title: Water Where It Shouldn't Be
items.text: Stains on a ceiling, a soft spot in drywall, a musty smell in a closet, or a water bill that jumped without explanation. Hidden leaks do the most damage because they go unnoticed the longest.

items.title: Low or Uneven Water Pressure
items.text: A single fixture with weak flow is usually the fixture. Low pressure through the whole house points to a supply-side issue — a failing pressure-reducing valve, a leak, or mineral buildup in older lines.

items.title: Sewer Smell or Gurgling Drains
items.text: A sewer odor in the house, or a toilet that gurgles when the washer drains, means air and wastewater are going somewhere they shouldn't. This is a main-line warning sign and should be looked at quickly.

items.title: Water Heater Acting Up
items.text: Lukewarm water, hot water that runs out fast, rumbling or popping from the tank, rust-colored water, or moisture around the base. Most tank water heaters last [10–12] years; many homes built in St. Charles County in the [late 1990s and 2000s] are on their second or third unit, and a lot of those are due.

items.title: A Sump Pump You Haven't Thought About
items.text: If you haven't heard your sump pump run in a while, or you don't know how old it is, it's worth testing before the next heavy rain. Sump pumps in this area work hard, and a failed pump shows up as a flooded basement.
